span.label: THE CONCLUSION IS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, NOT ABOUT MEMORY: `the significance of voice in implicit memory is DEPENDENT ON THE LEVEL OF PROCESSING REQUIRED BY THE TASK and the acoustic environment.` Whether voice matters to implicit memory has no answer on its own - it has an answer per task. **So two studies of `auditory priming` that used different tasks are not measuring the same thing**, and a corpus that pools their effect sizes is pooling answers to different questions. The paper was designed to demonstrate exactly this: it swapped the task and the role of voice changed
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PRIOR LITERATURE ALREADY DISAGREED WITH ITSELF, BY TASK, AND THIS PAPER NAMES IT: `a voice change between a spoken word and its repetition has been shown to have a DETRIMENTAL EFFECT on auditory priming in STEM COMPLETION and WORD IDENTIFICATION ... BUT NOT IN LEXICAL DECISION.` Three tasks, all called auditory priming, two showing an effect of voice and one not. That is the observation the whole study is built on - not a puzzle to be resolved but a clue about what the tasks measure
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: VOICE REPETITION TURNS OUT TO BE NECESSARY, NOT MERELY HELPFUL: `Quotation withheld.` Word repetition was intact in that condition - the same words came back - and priming did not. At the level this task works on, repeating the word is not enough; the voice has to repeat too, which is a much stronger claim than voice being one contributor among several
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE DOSE-RESPONSE HAS A CROSSING VARIABLE, WHICH IS WHY THE DESIGN NEEDED A SECOND ROUND. Priming appeared `only in the one- and two-speaker conditions` and vanished at three and four - but voice FAMILIARITY falls as the number of speakers rises, so the two are confounded by construction. When familiarity was equated by pre-training, priming came back at three voices. **`Number of speakers` is therefore not the variable it appears to be**, and the paper takes it apart rather than reporting the monotone result it could have
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE TASK WAS CHOSEN TO DEFEAT A RESPONSE BIAS, WHICH IS AN ARGUMENT ABOUT MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ABOUT MEMORY. The introduction's charge against the standard tasks is that requiring participants to report whole words `renders priming dependent on the activation of whole words while focusing performance away from the acoustic component` - so the instrument was producing the word-level answer it kept finding. Phoneme monitoring forces attention below the word, and the result changes. A methodological objection of the same shape as Holcomb2005's against Kiefer, in a different literature
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
